subject: Post-call: Integration & Model Routing for Acme - follow-up

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps \u0018 Integration + Model routing (Acme)

Hi Alex / Ops team,

Thanks for taking the time today \u0018 great discussion. Quick recap from our end and suggested next steps so we can scope the PoC and architecture review: 

Summary of needs we heard:
- SDK + auth: you want a simple SDK integration but require strong auth (potentially mTLS for private deploys) and KMS support for key rotation.
- Routing & policies: route traffic by region, meet latency SLOs, and fall back to lower-cost model variants when tight cost windows hit.
- Structured output / tool calling: you plan to call internal tools (ticketing/search) and want structured outputs with schema validation and function-like tool calls.
- Embeddings & reranker: use embeddings for semantic retrieval and a lightweight reranker for top-k refinement.
- Ops: observability and tracing per-route, plus cost breakdown and per-token billing visibility.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Share an architecture draft (link below) and a short list of your hard constraints (QPS, p95/p99 latency targets, data residency).
2) Engineering sync (30-45m) next week to walk SDK auth options and model routing examples.
3) We\u0019ll prepare a configuration example (routing + fallback + batching) and a sandbox api key for your PoC.

Links & artifacts:
- Integration architecture (shared): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-acme-integration-arch

Please reply with preferred times for next week and the items from step #1 \u0019 that\u0019ll let us prepare the config & cost estimate.

Best,

Thanks Marissa \u0018 solid recap. A few clarifying questions before we sync with engineering: 

1) SDK & auth: can you summarize supported auth flows? We prefer OAuth for user-level calls and mTLS for server-to-server in our private environment \u0018 curious what you recommend for the sandbox PoC vs. production private deployment. Also: does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping?

2) Model routing config: is the routing expressed via console-only UI or can we manage it via an API/YAML that we can check into our infra repo? We\u0019d like to templatize routing policies and include them in our deployment pipelines.

3) Fallback chains & cost policies: can you share an example of a policy that enforces a p95 latency target but allows occasional fallbacks to cheaper models for best-effort requests?

4) Structured output / tool calling safety: what guards do you provide to prevent hallucinated tool invocations? We need strict schema validation for outputs that drive downstream workflows.

5) Embeddings/reranker: are embeddings generated by a dedicated model? How do you recommend running reranking (Redwood-hosted reranker vs client-side reranker)?

We\u2019ll aim to get you our QPS and latency goals before the call. Also attaching a draft SOW for your review (acme_sow_draft.pdf) \u0018 we\u2019d like to align on scope and timing.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps \u0018 Integration + Model routing (Acme)

Hi Alex \u0018 jumping in with technical answers and a concrete example you can iterate on.

Auth & SDK:
- SDKs: we provide official SDKs (python, node, java) and a REST API. SDKs support API keys, OAuth2 client credentials, and mutual TLS for private deployments.
- KMS/HSM: production private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM; hosted accounts can integrate with customer KMS for envelope keys.

Routing & policy model (example):
We recommend managing routing via YAML stored in your repo and applied via Redwood\u2019s infra API. Example (pseudo YAML):

# route: search-api
region: eu-west-1
priority_pipeline:
  - match: {latency_p95: <=150ms, cost_per_token: <=0.0008}
    model_chain: [redwood-llama-70b-q4, redwood-llama-13b-q4]
  - match: {latency_p95: <=300ms}
    model_chain: [redwood-llama-13b-q4, redwood-llama-7b-q4]
fallback_policy:
  - on_error: use_next_model_in_chain
  - on_capacity: route_to_region: us-west-2

Notes on enforcement:
- Policies are declarative and can be validated by CI. The infra API lets you push versions and rollback.
- We surface per-route metrics (p50/p95/p99, cost/token) so you can automate rollouts based on SLO adherence.

Structured output / tool-calling:
- Use function-calling / structured outputs with explicit JSON schema. Redwood supports schema validation and will reject outputs that don\u2019t match (or emit sanitized error payloads).
- For safety, include allow/deny lists of callable tools and rate-limits per-tool.

Embeddings & reranker:
- Best practice: use a dedicated embed model (we have redwood-embed-1) and store vectors in your vector DB (we can host a managed index).
- Reranking: two options \u0018 server-side reranker hosted by Redwood (low-latency, integrated) or export candidate scores and run your own reranker. For initial PoC we usually host the reranker to simplify integration.

Operational suggestions:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for prompt patterns to reduce cost and improve p95.
- Configure per-route batching windows (e.g., 10-30ms) to balance throughput vs latency.

I attached the integration architecture diagram we discussed (architecture-diagram.pdf) and a quickstart repo link in the Drive doc above. I can put together a sample routing YAML tailored to your QPS and latency numbers once you share them.

If helpful, we can run a short tech kick-off (30m) with your infra and security folks \u0018 propose Thurs 21 May 09:00-09:30 PT or Fri 22 May 10:00-10:30 PT.

Regards,
Dev Patel
